model: An INDEPENDENT model of the Choi et al. charge series: Kramers barrier crossing within a finite susceptible subpopulation. Shares nothing with the three-ODE compartment model -- no nuclear or cytoplasmic pools, no autoregulation, no transport, no clearance term.
form: f(t) = p . (1 - exp(-nu(q).t)),  nu(q) = nu0 . exp(-b.q)
rationale: A rare barrier crossing gives an exponential waiting time and therefore a constant hazard, which the earlier reanalysis found. A barrier height linear in charge gives a rate EXPONENTIAL in charge, by Kramers. A finite susceptible fraction p is what the compartment model means by cells differing in margin.

fit.data: 18 constructs, percent of fibril-bearing cells at 48 h, read from the preprint's prose
fit.comparison: their straight line in percent gives R2 = 0.871 on the same 18 points with 2 parameters; this gives 0.957 with 3, and each parameter is a physical quantity rather than a slope

what_it_explains: The apparent SATURATION of rate beyond q = -4, which the first reanalysis flagged as anomalous, is not saturation of the rate. It is f approaching its ceiling p = 22.8 %: the fastest construct's 24.6 % is 108 % of that ceiling. The underlying nucleation rate keeps rising by a constant factor of 2.58 per two charge units, from 0.0023 /h at q = +2 to 0.102 /h at q = -6. Their linear relationship in PERCENT is a property of the readout saturating, not of the mechanism.

held_out_test.method: fitted on the 48 h column alone, then asked to predict the 72 h column
held_out_test.honest_caveat: All three residuals are POSITIVE: the model systematically UNDERPREDICTS at 72 h. Either p is larger than 22.8 %, or the susceptible pool is not fixed and cells become susceptible over time. The fit is not vindicated by this test so much as bounded by it.

independent_corroboration.framework: Stochastic nucleation per cell, with cells as independent reaction vesicles and only the nucleation step controlling aggregate appearance, is established for other aggregating proteins -- polyglutamine in C. elegans muscle (PNAS 2021, 'independent nucleation events determine the progression of polyglutamine aggregation') and huntingtin exon 1 in cells (Nat. Chem. Biol., unimolecular nucleation). Both give the probability of aggregation by time t as 1 - exp(-t/<T>), the same functional form used here.
independent_corroboration.rate_constant: The C. elegans work reports a nucleation rate of about 0.01 per hour per cell at 1 mM intracellular protein. The TDP-43 rate fitted here spans 0.0023 /h at wild-type charge to 0.102 /h at the most negative, with 0.0059 /h at neutral charge. The published figure sits inside that range. Different protein, different organism, different laboratory, different method -- and the same order of magnitude.
independent_corroboration.what_is_NOT_corroborated: The finite susceptible subpopulation. The searched literature describes outcomes as mostly non-aggregated or fully aggregated cells, which is close to bimodal, but no model with an explicit susceptible fraction was found. That extension is the part the 72 h residuals question, and it is the part that is mine.
independent_corroboration.a_caution_taken_from_the_same_literature: A review warns that the lag time of a bulk in-vitro aggregation assay must not be read as a waiting time for nucleation. The earlier note cited the TDP-43 LCD lag phase of 31 h at 24 uM as a measured input; by this caution that figure is not a nucleation waiting time and should not be used as one.
